title: TypeScript Utility & Advanced Types: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes on TypeScript's built-in utility types, mapped and conditional types, infer, and satisfies: what each does, how to compose them, the usual mistakes, and a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Type Transformation Mental Model
points: Utility types are generic type-level functions: they take a type and return a new type, and they are erased at compile time (zero runtime cost)
Partial<T> makes every property optional, Required<T> makes every property required (strips ?), Readonly<T> marks every property readonly
Pick<T, K> keeps only the listed keys; Omit<T, K> drops the listed keys; both are built from mapped types
All of these are shallow: Partial<User> does not make nested objects optional, and Readonly<T> does not freeze nested properties
Interview-style rule: Readonly<T> is compile-time only; Object.freeze is the runtime guard

chapters.title: Utility Types in Everyday Use
points: Update payload: function update(id: string, patch: Partial<User>) accepts any subset of User fields
Public view: type PublicUser = Omit<User, 'password'> hides sensitive fields; Pick<User, 'id' | 'name'> whitelists instead
Record<K, V> builds an object type with keys K and values V: Record<'admin' | 'user', Permissions> forces every key to be present
Record<string, V> is an index signature; with noUncheckedIndexedAccess on, lookups return V | undefined
Omit<T, K> does not check that K is a key of T (K extends keyof any), so a typo like Omit<User, 'pasword'> compiles silently and omits nothing

chapters.title: Function Types: ReturnType, Parameters, infer
points: ReturnType<typeof fn> extracts a function's return type; pass typeof fn, not fn: ReturnType<fn> is an error
Parameters<typeof fn> returns the parameter list as a tuple; index it with Parameters<typeof fn>[0] for the first argument
Awaited<ReturnType<typeof asyncFn>> unwraps the Promise, because ReturnType of an async function is Promise<T>
infer declares a type variable inside the extends clause of a conditional type: T extends (...args: any[]) => infer R ? R : never
ReturnType is just a conditional type with infer; infer is only legal in the extends clause and is pattern matching on the type's shape

chapters.title: Mapped Types and Conditional Types
points: Mapped type syntax: { [K in keyof T]: T[K] } loops over the keys of T; Partial<T> is { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }
Modifiers: add or remove with + and -: { [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] } is Required<T>; -readonly strips readonly
Key remapping with as: { [K in keyof T as `get${Capitalize<K & string>}`]: () => T[K] } renames keys; mapping a key to never via as drops it
Conditional type: T extends U ? X : Y; when T is a naked type parameter it distributes over a union, so ToArray<string | number> gives string[] | number[]
Wrap both sides in a tuple to stop distribution: [T] extends [U] ? X : Y; this is also how you test for never, because a distributive conditional on never yields never

chapters.title: satisfies and Common Mistakes
points: satisfies (TS 4.9) checks an expression against a type without widening it: const c = { red: [255,0,0] } satisfies Record<string, number[] | string> keeps red as number[]
Type annotation vs satisfies: annotation (const c: T) widens the value to T and loses specific property types; satisfies validates and keeps the literal inferred type
satisfies catches typos and missing keys at the declaration while keeping autocomplete for the exact keys; combine with as const to keep literal and readonly types
Mistake: assuming Partial, Readonly or Required are deep; use a recursive mapped type (DeepPartial<T>) when nesting matters
Mistake: using Omit on a union type, since it collapses the union's variants; use a distributive version: T extends any ? Omit<T, K> : never

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Utility and Advanced Types
points: Property modifiers: Partial<T> (all optional), Required<T> (all required), Readonly<T> (all readonly); all shallow
Key selection: Pick<T, 'a' | 'b'> keeps, Omit<T, 'a'> drops, Record<K, V> builds from a key union
Function extraction: ReturnType<typeof f>, Parameters<typeof f>, Awaited<...> for promises
Mapped type template: { [K in keyof T as NewKey]+?/-?: T[K] } with +/- readonly and ? modifiers
Conditional template: T extends U ? X : infer-capture; distributes over naked unions, [T] extends [U] does not; satisfies validates without widening
